title: Proper coincidence for native derived Weil direct images
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the categories $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(-)$ and the actual equivariant derived operations $h^*,Rh_*,Rh_{0!}$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let $h:V\to W$ be a proper morphism of $k_0$-schemes, with $W$ quasi-compact, quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k_0$. Then there is a natural isomorphism
$$Rh_{0!}\cong Rh_*:\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)\longrightarrow\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(W).$$

Actual source proofs have no local sorry; closure still needs the maintainer axiom audit. The native realization of proper coincidence in prop-functor-package clause 3.

proof.text: By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $h$ is separated and finite type. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], finite type means quasi-compact and locally finite type. Together with the assumptions on $W$, these verify the hypotheses of the chosen compactification in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Write it as $V\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{p}W$, with $pj=h$, $j$ open and $p$ proper. The properness definition makes $p$ separated and finite type too. Applying part (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] to $h$ and $p$ followed by $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ shows that $V$ and $Z$ are locally of finite type over $k_0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] over the base $W$, with proper $h:V\to W$, separated $p:Z\to W$ and $j:V\to Z$. It gives that $j$ is proper, hence universally closed. This needs no separatedness of $W$ over $k_0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-native-weil-clopen-sheaf-comparison] to this $j$. It gives an additive exact functor $j_!$ on the full abelian categories $\mathcal W$ and a natural isomorphism $\alpha_j:j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j_*$. For $u:M\to N$, naturality gives $j_*(u)=\alpha_{j,N}j_!(u)\alpha_{j,M}^{-1}$. Applying this to $u+v$ and using additivity of $j_!$ and bilinearity of composition proves additivity of $j_*$. For exactness put $G=j_!$, $H=j_*$ and $\alpha=\alpha_j$. If $k:A\to M$ is a kernel of $u$, then $Gk$ is a kernel of $Gu$. Given $t:S\to HM$ with $Hu\,t=0$, the map $\alpha_M^{-1}t$ is annihilated by $Gu$, hence factors uniquely through $Gk$; composing the factor with $\alpha_A$ gives the unique factor of $t$ through $Hk$. If $q:N\to C$ is a cokernel of $u$ and $t:HN\to S$ satisfies $tHu=0$, then $t\alpha_N$ factors uniquely through $Gq$, say as $bGq$; the required factor through $Hq$ is $b\alpha_C^{-1}$. Thus $H$ preserves kernels and cokernels and is exact. These are assertions about the native equivariant sheaves themselves.

proof.text: For $T=V,Z,W$ (locally of finite type by step 1) the native category $\mathcal W_T$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sf-native-weil-constructible-abelian]. Hence every complex there has a K-injective resolution by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective], so the hypothesis of [def-sfb-right-derived-exact] is available. Write $D(j_!)$ and $D(j_*)$ for termwise application localized at quasi-isomorphisms. For either exact functor $G=j_!,j_*$, preservation of kernels, images and cokernels gives a canonical isomorphism $H^a(GC)\cong G(H^a(C))$, natural in $C$. For a quasi-isomorphism $u$, naturality identifies $H^a(Gu)$ with $G(H^a(u))$ up to these isomorphisms, so $Gu$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Let $G_K:K(\mathcal W_V)\to K(\mathcal W_Z)$ be degreewise $G$ modulo chain homotopy and $Q_T:K(\mathcal W_T)\to D(\mathcal W_T)$ the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The functor $Q_Z\circ G_K$ therefore inverts quasi-isomorphisms; it factors through $Q_V$. Apply [def-sfb-right-derived-exact] to the exact functor $j_*$ to obtain $Rj_*\cong D(j_*)$. The degreewise isomorphism $\alpha_j$ of step 2 commutes with differentials by its naturality, so it defines an isomorphism of complexes natural in chain maps. Additivity of $j_!$ and $j_*$ makes both degreewise functors preserve chain homotopies: applying either functor $G$ to $u-v=ds+sd$ gives $G(u)-G(v)=G(d)G(s)+G(s)G(d)$. They therefore induce the required functors and comparison on homotopy categories. Apply $Q_Z$ to that comparison. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] lifts it and its inverse to mutually inverse natural transformations $D(j_!)\cong D(j_*)$; they remain inverse because that clause respects identities and composition. Write $a:D(j_!)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(j_*)$ for this lift and $\epsilon:Rj_*\xrightarrow{\sim}D(j_*)$ for exact derivation. Then $\theta=\epsilon^{-1}a:D(j_!)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_*$, with inverse $a^{-1}\epsilon$, on the ambient derived categories.

proof.text:
By [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], $Rh_{0!}=Rp_*D(j_!)$. Whisker $\theta$ with $Rp_*$ and apply the inverse of the natural isomorphism $c_{p,j}:R(pj)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*Rj_*$ of clause (a) of [lem-sf-native-weil-basic-comparisons], taken with $u=j$, $v=p$ between the locally finite-type schemes $V,Z,W$ of step 1 and on the whole unbounded native derived categories, using $pj=h$:
$$Rp_*D(j_!)\xrightarrow{\beta=Rp_*\theta}Rp_*Rj_*\xrightarrow{\delta=c_{p,j}^{-1}}Rh_*.$$
These are natural isomorphisms on $D(\mathcal W_V)$. Put $A=Rp_*D(j_!)$, $B=Rp_*Rj_*$ and $C=Rh_*$. For $u:K\to L$, the two naturality identities give
$$C(u)\delta_K\beta_K=\delta_L B(u)\beta_K=\delta_L\beta_L A(u).$$
Thus $\Phi_K=\delta_K\beta_K$ defines a natural transformation $Rh_{0!}\to Rh_*$. Its inverse has components $\beta_K^{-1}\delta_K^{-1}$: composing in either order cancels the adjacent inverse factors and yields the identity. Its naturality follows from the same displayed identity by multiplying on the left by $\Phi_L^{-1}$ and on the right by $\Phi_K^{-1}$. This proves a natural isomorphism of functors, including its inverse, on the ambient derived categories.

proof.text: As established in step 1, $h$ is separated and finite type. Thus it is quasi-compact and locally finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; $W$ has exactly the quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finite-type hypotheses in [lem-sf-native-weil-shriek-triangulated]. Its preservation clause therefore puts $Rh_{0!}K$ in $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(W)$ for every $K$ in $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)$. Since $Rh_*K$ is isomorphic to $Rh_{0!}K$ by step 4, it also has bounded constructible cohomology: cohomology takes this isomorphism to isomorphisms, which preserve vanishing. On each member $U$ of a pro-etale covering in the constructibility definition, compose its given trivialization with the restricted cohomology isomorphism to obtain the same $B_U^{\oplus r_U}$ trivialization for the new sheaf. The finite rank $r_U$ may depend on $U$, exactly as in the current framework; no uniform rank is required. The categories in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] are full subcategories of their ambient derived categories. Hence each $\Phi_K$ and its inverse are morphisms in those subcategories, and the naturality equation in step 4 is the same equation there. They give the asserted natural isomorphism between the restricted functors.
